title: First light
disclosure: Project-authored synthetic route. It is not anatomy and carries no clinical meaning.

stages.label: Approach
stages.guide: We are approaching a project-authored navigation model. It is intentionally synthetic, so it cannot teach anatomy.
stages.engineering: Procedural calibration geometry only. There are no structure IDs, ontology mappings, patient data, or pathophysiology claims.

stages.label: Surface trace
stages.guide: The dawn line marks one route through the model. The guide, camera, and moving signals all follow that same line.
stages.engineering: One normalized lookup drives the camera rail, guide geometry, corridor sweep, and analytic instances.

stages.label: Portal
stages.guide: The threshold changes our scale without pretending that one mesh spans every level. Reduced motion uses a direct cut here.
stages.engineering: An explicit semantic stage owns the transition. A bounded portal blend hands off to an opaque fog swap when motion is reduced.

stages.label: Flow corridor
stages.guide: These lights are flow markers, not blood cells. They show that thousands of signals can move smoothly without changing the route.
stages.engineering: Static phase, radial, speed, and seed attributes are sampled in a vertex shader from uniform time; no per-frame CPU instance matrices.

stages.label: Arrival
stages.guide: First light is complete. The voyage system is ready; anatomy and clinical teaching remain locked until separate evidence and human review exist.
stages.engineering: P0 engineering acceptance only. Asset adoption, medical content, and clinical publication remain fail-closed in provenance.
